html:
In the app

File → New Project… → A graded level → 21. Guided mode opens on this chapter: the tags, every rung below under its fold, a Verify check, and the run results. File → Load Reference Solution loads the program printed here.

Level 11 made three batches of one family of recipes in one tank. A real kitchen changes product, and the change is where the trouble is. Level 21 is Level 11’s kitchen making two batches of Soda (water and cola syrup, 5:1) and then two of Juice (water and orange concentrate, 3:1). Between them comes the changeover, and three things about it are new. The tank’s outlet sits above the bottom, so the outlet pump leaves a heel, five per cent of the tank, that carries the last batch into the next one unless it is rinsed out. The syrup tote has to be swapped for the concentrate tote, by an operator, and only when the tank is down to its heel. And the recipe changes: not just the amounts, but how you dose them, because a heel in the tank means topping up to the HI probe no longer gives you the ratio.

The machine

How the level is scored

What happensPoints
Each batch: the ratio within 5 % of the recipe+100 / −50
Each batch: the temperature at drain within −3 / +8 °F+100 / −50
Each batch: mixed at least the recipe time+100 / −50
A batch with more than 0.5 % of the other product in it−200
A short batch (under 80 % of the tank), an overflow, a scorched batch−50, −100, −100
Four batches out under par (270 s)+200

The recipes are the plant’s: Soda 83 % water at 100 °F, mixed 8 s; Juice 75 % water at 160 °F, mixed 10 s. Without a rinse the Juice carries about 1 % cola out of the heel, twice the limit.

Why the heel changes the dosing

Level 11 dosed A by counting its flowmeter and topped up with B to the HI probe: the ratio came out of the probe’s height. With 100 units of the last batch already in the tank, the probe is reached 100 units sooner, and whatever B is short, the ratio is off. So Level 21 doses both ingredients by their flowmeters, to counts the recipe rungs set, and the HI probe is left to the Full lamp. That is also the honest way: a recipe is amounts, not levels.

Tags this lesson needs

The alias tags of the machine are made for you; create these before you type the rungs. Verify reports any you miss.

Run and the two recipes

Step 0: at the heel, batch or changeover

Dose, heat, mix, drain

The changeover: rinse, swap, new set-up

The lamps

Run it

Load the program, Run mode, Start. Two Soda batches, each about 37 s. The selector turns to JUICE as the second drains; the tank fills to 30 % with water, mixes five seconds, drains, the lamp lights, the orange tote comes in and TOTE OK is pressed; two Juice batches at 160 °F, each a minute, because the heater has twice as far to go. 4 of 4 bottles in the right bin, nothing lost, in about 220 s against a par of 270 s: 1400 points and three stars.

rungs.head: Rung 0
rungs.comment: RUN: the seal-in, from the console buttons or the START and STOP on the HMI touch screen

pred.q: Start_PB is on, HMI_Start is on, Run is off, Stop_PB is off, HMI_Stop is off and E_Stop is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Run is on.

rungs.words: When either (Start_PB (Start push button, momentary) is on), (HMI_Start (START on the Tank_HMI touch screen (pulsed by the HMI)) is on) or (Run (Seal-in run bit) is on), Stop_PB (Stop push button, momentary) is off, HMI_Stop (STOP on the Tank_HMI touch screen (pulsed by the HMI)) is off and E_Stop (E-stop, NC: 1 = healthy) is on, the rung turns Run on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 3 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Start_PB) Examine If Closed asks: true when Start_PB is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(HMI_Start) Examine If Closed asks: true when HMI_Start is on.
    Path 3
    1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIO(Stop_PB) Examine If Open asks: true when Stop_PB is off.
  3. XIO(HMI_Stop) Examine If Open asks: true when HMI_Stop is off.
  4. XIC(E_Stop) Examine If Closed asks: true when E_Stop is on.
  5. OTE(Run) Output Energize does: turns Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.why: The start condition turns Run on, and Run’s own contact in the parallel path keeps the rung true after the start goes away. Anything in series outside the branch (a stop, a fault) breaks it, and then it stays off until the start is made again.
pats.think: a doorbell button and a hand. The start button is the doorbell, pressed for a moment. The seal-in contact is a hand that grabs the circuit as soon as the output comes on and keeps holding after you let go. The stop button, in series, is the only thing that can knock that hand away.
pats.watch: The stop has to be in series outside the branch. Put it inside the start path only and the seal-in path bypasses it: the stop no longer stops.

rungs.head: Rung 1
rungs.comment: RECIPE SODA: water and cola syrup 5:1. 71 pulses of water (1420 units) and 15 of syrup (300): 82.6 % water; 100 °F; mix 8 s. Both by flowmeter: the 5 % heel left in the tank would throw a top-up to the HI probe
rungs.words: When Sel_Juice (Product selector at JUICE (right); 0 = SODA) is off, the rung puts 71 into Target_A (Pulses of A for the selected product), puts 15 into Target_B (Pulses of B for the selected product), puts 100 into Target_T (Temperature for the selected product, °F) and puts 8000 into Mix_Pre (Mixing time for the selected product, ms).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(Sel_Juice) Examine If Open asks: true when Sel_Juice is off.
  2. A branch of 4 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. MOV(71,Target_A) Move does: puts 71 into Target_A. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 2
    1. MOV(15,Target_B) Move does: puts 15 into Target_B. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 3
    1. MOV(100,Target_T) Move does: puts 100 into Target_T. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 4
    1. MOV(8000,Mix_Pre) Move does: puts 8000 into Mix_Pre. It writes every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: Rung 2
rungs.comment: RECIPE JUICE: water and orange concentrate 3:1. 64 pulses of water (1280) and 21 of concentrate (420): 75.3 %; 160 °F; mix 10 s

pred.q: Sel_Juice is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Target_A is not written (it keeps its value), Target_B is not written (it keeps its value), Target_T is not written (it keeps its value) and Mix_Pre is not written (it keeps its value). It stops at XIC(Sel_Juice).

rungs.words: When Sel_Juice (Product selector at JUICE (right); 0 = SODA) is on, the rung puts 64 into Target_A (Pulses of A for the selected product), puts 21 into Target_B (Pulses of B for the selected product), puts 160 into Target_T (Temperature for the selected product, °F) and puts 10000 into Mix_Pre (Mixing time for the selected product, ms).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Sel_Juice) Examine If Closed asks: true when Sel_Juice is on.
  2. A branch of 4 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. MOV(64,Target_A) Move does: puts 64 into Target_A. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 2
    1. MOV(21,Target_B) Move does: puts 21 into Target_B. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 3
    1. MOV(160,Target_T) Move does: puts 160 into Target_T. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 4
    1. MOV(10000,Mix_Pre) Move does: puts 10000 into Mix_Pre. It writes every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: Rung 3
rungs.comment: Hysteresis: heat on below the target minus 2 °F, off at the target
rungs.words: Every scan, the rung makes Target_Lo (Heater comes back on below this, °F) = Target_T (Temperature for the selected product, °F) − 2.
rungs.ltr: 1. SUB(Target_T,2,Target_Lo) Subtract does: makes Target_Lo = Target_T − 2. Every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: Rung 4
rungs.comment: STEP 0: counters and the mixing timer start from nothing. This rung sits above the one that leaves step 0, so it runs in the scan the step is 0; below it, it would never see a 0

pred.q: Step is 0. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: A_Count is reset, B_Count is reset and Mix_T is reset.

rungs.words: When Step (Step: 0 wait at the heel, 1 dose A, 2 dose B, 3 heat and mix, 4 drain; 5 rinse fill, 6 rinse mix, 7 rinse drain, 8 tote swap) equals 0, the rung resets A_Count (Flowmeter A pulses this batch), resets B_Count (Flowmeter B pulses this batch) and resets Mix_T (Mixing time this batch).
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,0) Equal asks: true when Step equals 0. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. A branch of 3 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. RES(A_Count) Reset does: resets A_Count. It zeroes a timer or counter (accumulator and status bits), or a control (its position and status bits).
    Path 2
    1. RES(B_Count) Reset does: resets B_Count. It zeroes a timer or counter (accumulator and status bits), or a control (its position and status bits).
    Path 3
    1. RES(Mix_T) Reset does: resets Mix_T. It zeroes a timer or counter (accumulator and status bits), or a control (its position and status bits).

rungs.head: Rung 5
rungs.comment: STEP 0 → 1 or 5: the tank is down to its heel (the level reads 5, not 0: the outlet sits above the bottom). If the selector asks for the other product than the tank is set up for, go to the changeover (step 5); otherwise start a batch (step 1)
rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on, Step (Step: 0 wait at the heel, 1 dose A, 2 dose B, 3 heat and mix, 4 drain; 5 rinse fill, 6 rinse mix, 7 rinse drain, 8 tote swap) equals 0, Lo_Level (LO probe covered (10 %)) is off and Tank_Level (Tank level 0-100 %) is at most 5, each path is tested on its own: if Sel_Juice (Product selector at JUICE (right); 0 = SODA) is on and Cur_Juice (The tank and the tote are set up for Juice (0: Soda)) is off, it puts 5 into Step; if Sel_Juice is off and Cur_Juice is on, it puts 5 into Step; if Sel_Juice is on and Cur_Juice is on, it puts 1 into Step; if Sel_Juice is off and Cur_Juice is off, it puts 1 into Step.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. EQU(Step,0) Equal asks: true when Step equals 0. Both values are compared every scan.
  3. XIO(Lo_Level) Examine If Open asks: true when Lo_Level is off.
  4. LEQ(Tank_Level,5) Less Than or Equal asks: true when Tank_Level is at most 5.
  5. A branch of 4 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Sel_Juice) Examine If Closed asks: true when Sel_Juice is on.
    2. XIO(Cur_Juice) Examine If Open asks: true when Cur_Juice is off.
    3. MOV(5,Step) Move does: puts 5 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 2
    1. XIO(Sel_Juice) Examine If Open asks: true when Sel_Juice is off.
    2. XIC(Cur_Juice) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cur_Juice is on.
    3. MOV(5,Step) Move does: puts 5 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 3
    1. XIC(Sel_Juice) Examine If Closed asks: true when Sel_Juice is on.
    2. XIC(Cur_Juice) Examine If Closed asks: true when Cur_Juice is on.
    3. MOV(1,Step) Move does: puts 1 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 4
    1. XIO(Sel_Juice) Examine If Open asks: true when Sel_Juice is off.
    2. XIO(Cur_Juice) Examine If Open asks: true when Cur_Juice is off.
    3. MOV(1,Step) Move does: puts 1 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (Step = 0, to 5); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.
pats.think: a recipe card with numbered steps and one finger on it. Each rung only reads the line under the finger; when its line is done it moves the finger to the next number.
pats.watch: A rung further down that tests for the new step number sees it in this same scan. Rung order decides whether the next step starts now or next scan.

rungs.head: Rung 6
rungs.comment: STEP 1: dose the water. Step 5, the rinse fill, runs the same pump, so it is in this one rung: a second OTE(Pump_A) further down would win every scan and this one would never run

pred.q: Run is on and Step is 2. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Pump_A is off. None of the branch’s paths is true.

rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on and either (Step (Step: 0 wait at the heel, 1 dose A, 2 dose B, 3 heat and mix, 4 drain; 5 rinse fill, 6 rinse mix, 7 rinse drain, 8 tote swap) equals 1) or (Step equals 5), the rung turns Pump_A (Ingredient A pump) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. EQU(Step,1) Equal asks: true when Step equals 1. Both values are compared every scan.
    Path 2
    1. EQU(Step,5) Equal asks: true when Step equals 5. Both values are compared every scan.
  3. OTE(Pump_A) Output Energize does: turns Pump_A on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 7
rungs.comment: Count flowmeter A: one edge per 20 units
rungs.words: When Flow_A (Flowmeter A pulses (20 units each)) is on, the rung counts A_Count (Flowmeter A pulses this batch) up by one (preset 9999).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Flow_A) Examine If Closed asks: true when Flow_A is on.
  2. CTU(A_Count,9999,0) Count Up does: counts A_Count up by one (preset 9999). It counts false-to-true transitions of the rung, not scans; .DN is on once the count reaches the preset.

pats.t: A counter: one count per false-to-true.
pats.why: A_Count counts transitions of the rung, not scans, so a part that sits in front of an eye for a second counts once.
pats.think: a clicker at a door: one click per person coming in, however slowly they walk through.
pats.watch: A counter keeps its count until a RES. If the count should start again at each batch, something has to reset it.

rungs.head: Rung 8
rungs.comment: Water dosed: on to B

pred.q: Step is 1, A_Count.ACC is 38 and Target_A is 29. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Step is written.

rungs.words: When Step (Step: 0 wait at the heel, 1 dose A, 2 dose B, 3 heat and mix, 4 drain; 5 rinse fill, 6 rinse mix, 7 rinse drain, 8 tote swap) equals 1 and A_Count.ACC (the accumulated value of A_Count: Flowmeter A pulses this batch) is at least Target_A (Pulses of A for the selected product), the rung puts 2 into Step.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,1) Equal asks: true when Step equals 1. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. GEQ(A_Count.ACC,Target_A) Greater Than or Equal asks: true when A_Count.ACC is at least Target_A.
  3. MOV(2,Step) Move does: puts 2 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (Step = 1, to 2); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.

rungs.head: Rung 9
rungs.comment: STEP 2: dose the syrup or the concentrate, by count, not to the probe
rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on and Step (Step: 0 wait at the heel, 1 dose A, 2 dose B, 3 heat and mix, 4 drain; 5 rinse fill, 6 rinse mix, 7 rinse drain, 8 tote swap) equals 2, the rung turns Pump_B (Ingredient B pump) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. EQU(Step,2) Equal asks: true when Step equals 2. Both values are compared every scan.
  3. OTE(Pump_B) Output Energize does: turns Pump_B on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 10
rungs.comment: Count flowmeter B
rungs.words: When Flow_B (Flowmeter B pulses (20 units each)) is on, the rung counts B_Count (Flowmeter B pulses this batch) up by one (preset 9999).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Flow_B) Examine If Closed asks: true when Flow_B is on.
  2. CTU(B_Count,9999,0) Count Up does: counts B_Count up by one (preset 9999). It counts false-to-true transitions of the rung, not scans; .DN is on once the count reaches the preset.

pats.t: A counter: one count per false-to-true.
pats.why: B_Count counts transitions of the rung, not scans, so a part that sits in front of an eye for a second counts once.

rungs.head: Rung 11
rungs.comment: B dosed: heat and mix
rungs.words: When Step (Step: 0 wait at the heel, 1 dose A, 2 dose B, 3 heat and mix, 4 drain; 5 rinse fill, 6 rinse mix, 7 rinse drain, 8 tote swap) equals 2 and B_Count.ACC (the accumulated value of B_Count: Flowmeter B pulses this batch) is at least Target_B (Pulses of B for the selected product), the rung puts 3 into Step.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,2) Equal asks: true when Step equals 2. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. GEQ(B_Count.ACC,Target_B) Greater Than or Equal asks: true when B_Count.ACC is at least Target_B.
  3. MOV(3,Step) Move does: puts 3 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (Step = 2, to 3); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.

rungs.head: Rung 12
rungs.comment: STEP 3: mix (and step 6, the rinse mix: one OTE per output)

pred.q: Run is on and Step is 4. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Mixer is off. None of the branch’s paths is true.

rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on and either (Step (Step: 0 wait at the heel, 1 dose A, 2 dose B, 3 heat and mix, 4 drain; 5 rinse fill, 6 rinse mix, 7 rinse drain, 8 tote swap) equals 3) or (Step equals 6), the rung turns Mixer (Mixer motor) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. EQU(Step,3) Equal asks: true when Step equals 3. Both values are compared every scan.
    Path 2
    1. EQU(Step,6) Equal asks: true when Step equals 6. Both values are compared every scan.
  3. OTE(Mixer) Output Energize does: turns Mixer on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 13
rungs.comment: Mixing time: the preset is a tag the recipe rung sets
rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on and Step (Step: 0 wait at the heel, 1 dose A, 2 dose B, 3 heat and mix, 4 drain; 5 rinse fill, 6 rinse mix, 7 rinse drain, 8 tote swap) equals 3, the rung runs the timer Mix_T (Mixing time this batch) toward Mix_Pre.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. EQU(Step,3) Equal asks: true when Step equals 3. Both values are compared every scan.
  3. TON(Mix_T,Mix_Pre,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer Mix_T toward Mix_Pre. The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: Mix_T counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.
pats.think: a kitchen timer you have to keep holding down. Let go and it springs back to zero.
pats.watch: A rung that resets its own timer’s condition (a timer that cuts its own rung with its .DN) restarts every preset: that is a pulse generator, not a delay. Make sure that is what you meant.

rungs.head: Rung 14
rungs.comment: HEATER with hysteresis: on below the target minus 2

pred.q: Step is 3, Tank_Temp is 14 and Target_Lo is 37. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Heat_On latches on.

rungs.words: When Step (Step: 0 wait at the heel, 1 dose A, 2 dose B, 3 heat and mix, 4 drain; 5 rinse fill, 6 rinse mix, 7 rinse drain, 8 tote swap) equals 3 and Tank_Temp (Tank temperature, °F) is less than Target_Lo (Heater comes back on below this, °F), the rung latches Heat_On (Heater wanted (with hysteresis)) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,3) Equal asks: true when Step equals 3. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. LES(Tank_Temp,Target_Lo) Less Than asks: true when Tank_Temp is less than Target_Lo.
  3. OTL(Heat_On) Output Latch does: latches Heat_On on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Heat_On stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.
pats.think: a light switch rather than a doorbell: flick it on and it stays on until someone flicks it off.
pats.watch: A latched bit survives a stop, and it survives a download that keeps tag values. If nothing ever unlatches it, the machine remembers a state that is long gone.

rungs.head: Rung 15
rungs.comment: off at the target, outside step 3, or at the high limit
rungs.words: When either (Tank_Temp (Tank temperature, °F) is at least Target_T (Temperature for the selected product, °F)), (Step (Step: 0 wait at the heel, 1 dose A, 2 dose B, 3 heat and mix, 4 drain; 5 rinse fill, 6 rinse mix, 7 rinse drain, 8 tote swap) is not 3) or (Thermostat (High-limit thermostat, closes at 180 °F) is on), the rung unlatches Heat_On (Heater wanted (with hysteresis)).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 3 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. GEQ(Tank_Temp,Target_T) Greater Than or Equal asks: true when Tank_Temp is at least Target_T.
    Path 2
    1. NEQ(Step,3) Not Equal asks: true when Step is not 3.
    Path 3
    1. XIC(Thermostat) Examine If Closed asks: true when Thermostat is on.
  2. OTU(Heat_On) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Heat_On. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Heat_On when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 16
rungs.comment: Never heat an uncovered element (Lo_Level) or past the high-limit thermostat

pred.q: Run is off, Heat_On is off, Lo_Level is off and Thermostat is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Heater is off. It stops at XIC(Run).

rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on, Heat_On (Heater wanted (with hysteresis)) is on, Lo_Level (LO probe covered (10 %)) is on and Thermostat (High-limit thermostat, closes at 180 °F) is off, the rung turns Heater (Heater element) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIC(Heat_On) Examine If Closed asks: true when Heat_On is on.
  3. XIC(Lo_Level) Examine If Closed asks: true when Lo_Level is on.
  4. XIO(Thermostat) Examine If Open asks: true when Thermostat is off.
  5. OTE(Heater) Output Energize does: turns Heater on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 17
rungs.comment: Mixed long enough and at temperature: drain
rungs.words: When Step (Step: 0 wait at the heel, 1 dose A, 2 dose B, 3 heat and mix, 4 drain; 5 rinse fill, 6 rinse mix, 7 rinse drain, 8 tote swap) equals 3, Mix_T.DN (the done bit of Mix_T: Mixing time this batch) is on and Tank_Temp (Tank temperature, °F) is at least Target_Lo (Heater comes back on below this, °F), the rung puts 4 into Step.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,3) Equal asks: true when Step equals 3. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIC(Mix_T.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Mix_T.DN is on.
  3. GEQ(Tank_Temp,Target_Lo) Greater Than or Equal asks: true when Tank_Temp is at least Target_Lo.
  4. MOV(4,Step) Move does: puts 4 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (Step = 3, to 4); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.

rungs.head: Rung 18
rungs.comment: STEP 4 (and the rinse drain, step 7): the outlet pump. It stops drawing at the heel

pred.q: Run is on and Step is 4. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Pump_Out is on.

rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on and either (Step (Step: 0 wait at the heel, 1 dose A, 2 dose B, 3 heat and mix, 4 drain; 5 rinse fill, 6 rinse mix, 7 rinse drain, 8 tote swap) equals 4) or (Step equals 7), the rung turns Pump_Out (Outlet pump) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. EQU(Step,4) Equal asks: true when Step equals 4. Both values are compared every scan.
    Path 2
    1. EQU(Step,7) Equal asks: true when Step equals 7. Both values are compared every scan.
  3. OTE(Pump_Out) Output Energize does: turns Pump_Out on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 19
rungs.comment: The level reads the heel: run the pump on a second to be sure the batch is out
rungs.words: When either (Step (Step: 0 wait at the heel, 1 dose A, 2 dose B, 3 heat and mix, 4 drain; 5 rinse fill, 6 rinse mix, 7 rinse drain, 8 tote swap) equals 4) or (Step equals 7) and Tank_Level (Tank level 0-100 %) is at most 5, the rung runs the timer Empty_T (Run the outlet pump on a moment once the level reads the heel) toward 1000 ms (1 s).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. EQU(Step,4) Equal asks: true when Step equals 4. Both values are compared every scan.
    Path 2
    1. EQU(Step,7) Equal asks: true when Step equals 7. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. LEQ(Tank_Level,5) Less Than or Equal asks: true when Tank_Level is at most 5.
  3. TON(Empty_T,1000,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer Empty_T toward 1000 ms (1 s). The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: Empty_T counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.

rungs.head: Rung 20
rungs.comment: Batch out: count it, back to step 0
rungs.words: When Step (Step: 0 wait at the heel, 1 dose A, 2 dose B, 3 heat and mix, 4 drain; 5 rinse fill, 6 rinse mix, 7 rinse drain, 8 tote swap) equals 4, Empty_T.DN (the done bit of Empty_T: Run the outlet pump on a moment once the level reads the heel) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung makes Batch_Count (Batches made: the BATCHES display) = Batch_Count + 1 and puts 0 into Step.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,4) Equal asks: true when Step equals 4. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIC(Empty_T.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Empty_T.DN is on.
  3. ONS(Done_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Done_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  4. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. ADD(Batch_Count,1,Batch_Count) Add does: makes Batch_Count = Batch_Count + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.
    Path 2
    1. MOV(0,Step) Move does: puts 0 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (Step = 4, to 0); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
pats.think: a turnstile. However long you stand in it, it counts you once.
pats.watch: Each one-shot needs its own storage bit. Two one-shots sharing a bit fight over it, and one of them never fires.

rungs.head: Rung 21
rungs.comment: CHANGEOVER, STEP 5: rinse fill (Pump_A runs from the step 1 rung). Enough water to swill the heel out: 30 %
rungs.words: When Step (Step: 0 wait at the heel, 1 dose A, 2 dose B, 3 heat and mix, 4 drain; 5 rinse fill, 6 rinse mix, 7 rinse drain, 8 tote swap) equals 5 and Tank_Level (Tank level 0-100 %) is at least 30, the rung puts 6 into Step.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,5) Equal asks: true when Step equals 5. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. GEQ(Tank_Level,30) Greater Than or Equal asks: true when Tank_Level is at least 30.
  3. MOV(6,Step) Move does: puts 6 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (Step = 5, to 6); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.

rungs.head: Rung 22
rungs.comment: STEP 6: mix the rinse five seconds (the Mixer runs from the step 3 rung) so the heel is in the water, not under it

pred.q: Run is off and Step is 6. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Rinse_T is reset to 0. It stops at XIC(Run).

rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on and Step (Step: 0 wait at the heel, 1 dose A, 2 dose B, 3 heat and mix, 4 drain; 5 rinse fill, 6 rinse mix, 7 rinse drain, 8 tote swap) equals 6, the rung runs the timer Rinse_T (Rinse mixing time) toward 5000 ms (5 s).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. EQU(Step,6) Equal asks: true when Step equals 6. Both values are compared every scan.
  3. TON(Rinse_T,5000,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer Rinse_T toward 5000 ms (5 s). The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: Rinse_T counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.

rungs.head: Rung 23
rungs.comment: rinsed: drain it
rungs.words: When Step (Step: 0 wait at the heel, 1 dose A, 2 dose B, 3 heat and mix, 4 drain; 5 rinse fill, 6 rinse mix, 7 rinse drain, 8 tote swap) equals 6 and Rinse_T.DN (the done bit of Rinse_T: Rinse mixing time) is on, the rung puts 7 into Step and resets Rinse_T (Rinse mixing time).
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,6) Equal asks: true when Step equals 6. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIC(Rinse_T.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Rinse_T.DN is on.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. MOV(7,Step) Move does: puts 7 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 2
    1. RES(Rinse_T) Reset does: resets Rinse_T. It zeroes a timer or counter (accumulator and status bits), or a control (its position and status bits).

pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (Step = 6, to 7); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.

rungs.head: Rung 24
rungs.comment: STEP 7 → 8: the rinse is out (down to the heel again, now nearly all water)
rungs.words: When Step (Step: 0 wait at the heel, 1 dose A, 2 dose B, 3 heat and mix, 4 drain; 5 rinse fill, 6 rinse mix, 7 rinse drain, 8 tote swap) equals 7, Empty_T.DN (the done bit of Empty_T: Run the outlet pump on a moment once the level reads the heel) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung puts 8 into Step.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,7) Equal asks: true when Step equals 7. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIC(Empty_T.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Empty_T.DN is on.
  3. ONS(Rinse_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Rinse_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  4. MOV(8,Step) Move does: puts 8 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (Step = 7, to 8); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.

rungs.head: Rung 25
rungs.comment: STEP 8: ask for the tote swap. The lamp is only lit with the tank down to its heel, so the operator never swaps a tote on a tank with a batch in it
rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on and Step (Step: 0 wait at the heel, 1 dose A, 2 dose B, 3 heat and mix, 4 drain; 5 rinse fill, 6 rinse mix, 7 rinse drain, 8 tote swap) equals 8, the rung turns Lamp_Swap (Swap lamp: asks the operator to swap the syrup tote (with the tank down to its heel)) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. EQU(Step,8) Equal asks: true when Step equals 8. Both values are compared every scan.
  3. OTE(Lamp_Swap) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Swap on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 26
rungs.comment: TOTE OK: the tote is the new product; remember the set-up and go back to step 0, where the new recipe starts

pred.q: Tote_OK is on, Sel_Juice is on and Step is 8. What does the rung do?
pred.a: Power reaches only part of the rung: Cur_Juice latches on, Cur_Juice is left as it was and Step is written.

rungs.words: When Step (Step: 0 wait at the heel, 1 dose A, 2 dose B, 3 heat and mix, 4 drain; 5 rinse fill, 6 rinse mix, 7 rinse drain, 8 tote swap) equals 8 and Tote_OK (The operator has swapped the tote and pressed TOTE OK) is on, each path is tested on its own: if Sel_Juice (Product selector at JUICE (right); 0 = SODA) is on, it latches Cur_Juice (The tank and the tote are set up for Juice (0: Soda)) on; if Sel_Juice is off, it unlatches Cur_Juice; it puts 0 into Step.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,8) Equal asks: true when Step equals 8. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIC(Tote_OK) Examine If Closed asks: true when Tote_OK is on.
  3. A branch of 3 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Sel_Juice) Examine If Closed asks: true when Sel_Juice is on.
    2. OTL(Cur_Juice) Output Latch does: latches Cur_Juice on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.
    Path 2
    1. XIO(Sel_Juice) Examine If Open asks: true when Sel_Juice is off.
    2. OTU(Cur_Juice) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Cur_Juice. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 3
    1. MOV(0,Step) Move does: puts 0 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (Step = 8, to 0); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.
Cur_Juice stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 27
rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on, the rung turns Lamp_Run (Run lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. OTE(Lamp_Run) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 28

pred.q: Run is off and Step is 0. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Lamp_Idle is off. It stops at XIC(Run).

rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on and Step (Step: 0 wait at the heel, 1 dose A, 2 dose B, 3 heat and mix, 4 drain; 5 rinse fill, 6 rinse mix, 7 rinse drain, 8 tote swap) equals 0, the rung turns Lamp_Idle (Idle lamp: waiting for an empty tank or a Start) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. EQU(Step,0) Equal asks: true when Step equals 0. Both values are compared every scan.
  3. OTE(Lamp_Idle) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Idle on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 29
rungs.words: When Hi_Level (HI probe covered (90 %)) is on, the rung turns Lamp_Full (Full lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Hi_Level) Examine If Closed asks: true when Hi_Level is on.
  2. OTE(Lamp_Full) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Full on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 30
rungs.comment: The fault lamp: the high-limit thermostat is made

pred.q: Thermostat is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Lamp_Fault is on.

rungs.words: When Thermostat (High-limit thermostat, closes at 180 °F) is on, the rung turns Lamp_Fault (Fault lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Thermostat) Examine If Closed asks: true when Thermostat is on.
  2. OTE(Lamp_Fault) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Fault on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

HMI_Stop.desc: STOP on the Tank_HMI touch screen (pulsed by the HMI)

Target_B.desc: Pulses of B for the selected product

Mix_Pre.desc: Mixing time for the selected product, ms

Target_Lo.desc: Heater comes back on below this, °F
